title: Appendices
body:
## A. Glossary of US Power Market Terminology

**Baseload** — Generation that operates continuously at high capacity factors to serve the minimum layer of electricity demand; nuclear and large combined-cycle gas plants are canonical baseload assets because their economics reward sustained, high-utilisation dispatch.

**Capacity auction / capacity market** — PJM's annual administered Base Residual Auction (BRA) procures forward commitments from generators and demand-response providers to be available three years out; clearing prices are quoted in dollars per megawatt-day ($/MW-day) and paid across the delivery year regardless of whether the capacity is actually dispatched.

**Combined-cycle** — A natural gas technology that captures combustion-turbine exhaust heat in a heat-recovery steam generator to drive a second steam turbine; combined-cycle units achieve thermal efficiencies of 55–60%, making them the dispatchable workhorse of PJM's gas fleet.

**IPP (Independent Power Producer)** — A non-utility electricity generator selling into wholesale markets rather than under regulated cost-of-service structures; IPPs bear commodity price and dispatch risk that regulated utilities pass through to ratepayers.

**LCOE (Levelized Cost of Energy)** — The all-in average cost per megawatt-hour over an asset's operating life, capturing fuel, fixed and variable operating costs, and capital recovery; Susquehanna's implied LCOE of approximately $27/MWh places it among the most competitive baseload assets in the PJM footprint.

**MW-day** — The unit in which PJM capacity payments are expressed; one megawatt of committed capacity earns the clearing price multiplied by the days in the delivery period (typically 365).

**MWh (megawatt-hour)** — The standard unit of electrical energy; one megawatt of capacity running continuously for one hour produces one MWh.

**NRC (Nuclear Regulatory Commission)** — The US federal agency that licenses, inspects, and regulates civilian nuclear plants; NRC operating licence renewals and safety reviews are the primary regulatory gating events for nuclear generators.

**Peaking** — Simple-cycle gas turbines or fast-start capacity that runs only during demand peaks; high operating costs make peaking units uneconomic at baseload utilisation, but they earn scarcity rents during price spikes.

**PJM** — The regional transmission organisation coordinating wholesale electricity markets and transmission across thirteen Mid-Atlantic and Midwestern states plus the District of Columbia; it operates the largest competitive wholesale electricity market in the world by load.

**PPA (Power Purchase Agreement)** — A long-term bilateral contract under which a generator sells a defined volume of electricity — and, where structured, associated environmental attributes — to a buyer at a negotiated price or formula; the Amazon AWS nuclear PPA with Talen runs through 2042 at up to 1,920 MW.

**RMR (Reliability Must-Run)** — A PJM contract requiring a generator that would otherwise retire to remain available for system reliability; PJM compensates the unit at a cost-of-service rate independent of market prices. Talen's Brandon Shores ($145M/year) and H.A. Wagner ($35M/year) RMR contracts together provide $180M of fixed annual revenue through May 2029.

**SMR (Small Modular Reactor)** — A nuclear fission reactor with standardised, factory-fabricated components targeting sub-300 MW output; not yet commercially deployed in the United States, though Talen and Amazon have disclosed exploratory co-development discussions within Talen's Pennsylvania footprint.

## B. Generation Portfolio by Fuel Type and Capacity

Portfolio as of May 23, 2026, inclusive of Freedom and Guernsey (closed FY2025); Cornerstone (~$3.45B, agreed) is excluded pending close.

| Fuel / Technology | Capacity (GW) | Key Assets | Carbon Profile |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nuclear | 2.2 | Susquehanna Steam Electric Station (90% of 2.5 GW) | Carbon-free |
| Natural gas — combined-cycle | 2.8 | Freedom (PA), Guernsey (OH) | Low-carbon dispatchable |
| Intermediate / peaking | 4.6 | Various PJM-footprint units | Variable |
| Coal (minority interests) | ~0.8 | Minority stakes | Carbon-intensive |
| **Total (as reported)** | **~13.1** | | |
| *Low/zero-carbon baseload subtotal* | *5.7* | *Nuclear + qualifying CC units* | |

*Pro forma for Cornerstone close: approximately 15.5 GW, adding ~2.0 GW combined-cycle and 456 MW peaking.*
